tagline: Replace hardcoded values with named, reusable inputs — making data connections and transformations flexible and maintainable

slides.title: Why Parameters Matter in Power Query
slides.body: Power Query parameters are named values that can be reused across multiple queries and transformation steps. Instead of hardcoding a server name, folder path, date cutoff, or filter value directly in your M code, you define a parameter once and reference it everywhere. Parameters can be changed in one place to update all queries that reference them — critical for moving models between Development, Test, and Production environments or for user-configurable filtering.
slides.keyPoint: A parameter is a named, single-value placeholder. Changing the parameter value updates every query that references it — no need to find and replace hardcoded values across multiple steps.

slides.title: Common Parameter Use Cases
slides.caption: Parameters replace hardcoded values with reusable named references
rows: Environment parameter referenced in all 6 queries
slides.note: Parameters support types: Text, Number, Date, DateTime, Duration, Binary, Logical, Any. The type restricts what values can be assigned.

slides.title: Creating and Referencing a Parameter in M
slides.annotation: Parameters appear in the Queries pane alongside data queries. They are evaluated before any query runs — every query referencing the parameter sees the current value at refresh time.

slides.note: Using a parameter in a filter step (e.g., StartDate parameter in Table.SelectRows) typically preserves query folding — the value is passed as a literal to the WHERE clause.

slides.title: Dynamic Data Sources and Gateway Implications
bullets: When a data source connection uses a parameter (dynamic data source), Power BI may classify it as a 'dynamic data source'
Dynamic data sources cannot always use scheduled refresh in the Power BI Service without additional configuration
To avoid issues: use parameters only in filter steps AFTER the Source step, not in the Source connection itself, where possible
If parameters are used in Source connections, the gateway must be configured with the static source addresses — or use an on-premises gateway with credential mapping
The 'Skip Test Connection' option in data source settings can sometimes resolve dynamic source refresh errors
slides.keyPoint: Parameters in Source connection strings (server names, file paths) create dynamic data sources that may block scheduled refresh in the Power BI Service. This is a common PL-300 scenario — the fix is either static source connections or proper gateway configuration.

slides.title: PL-300 Exam — Key Facts
bullets: Parameters are created in Home > Manage Parameters in Power Query Editor
Parameters can be used in: Source connections, filter conditions, column name references, and as inputs to custom functions
A parameter referenced in a Source step makes the data source 'dynamic' — this can prevent scheduled refresh unless the gateway is configured to handle it
Parameters enable environment switching (Dev/Test/Prod) without editing each query — the standard enterprise approach to multi-environment deployment
Power BI Template (.pbit) files include parameter prompts — users fill in values when opening the template
slides.keyPoint: Parameters are the Power Query answer to hardcoded values — they enable flexible, maintainable, multi-environment M code. The exam tests both how to create them and the scheduling/gateway implications of dynamic sources.
